name: containerize-aspnet-framework
description: Containerize an ASP.NET .NET Framework project by creating customized Dockerfile and .dockerfile files.

Containerize the project in the settings below, focusing exclusively on changes required to run in a Windows Docker container. This is .NET Framework, not .NET Core. Unspecified settings use defaults.

Settings:
- Project: `[ProjectName (provide path to .csproj file)]`
- Windows Server SKU: `[Windows Server Core (Default) or Windows Server Full]`
- Windows Server version: `[2016, 2019, or 2022]`
- Custom build/run base images: `[None or image]`
- Ports: Primary HTTP `[e.g., 80]`; additional `[None or list]`
- Container user: `[account, default ContainerUser]`
- IIS settings: `[None or list]`
- Custom pre-/post-build steps: `[None or list]`
- GAC assemblies, MSIs, COM components, registry keys/values: `[None or list]`
- Environment variables: `[Use defaults or names/values]`
- Windows roles/features: `[None or list]`
- Files/directories to copy: `[None or paths relative to project root]`; target: `[container paths or Not applicable]`
- Exclusions and additional `.dockerignore` patterns: `[None or patterns]`
- Health check endpoint: `[None or URL path]`; interval/timeout: `[Use defaults or values]`
- Other requirements and known issues: `[None or details]`

✅ App configuration modification to use config builders for environment app settings and connection strings; Dockerfile creation; multiple build/publish stages; Windows compatibility; dependency handling.
❌ No infrastructure setup (handled separately).
❌ No code changes beyond those required for containerization.

Procedure:
1. Review settings.
2. Create `progress.md` with check marks.
3. Read `TargetFrameworkVersion` from the project `.csproj`.
4. Select the image using detected .NET Framework version and specified SKU/version. Tags: https://github.com/microsoft/dotnet-framework-docker/blob/main/README.aspnet.md#full-tag-listing
5. Required package: `Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.Environment`. **DO NOT** install these if they are missing. If they are not installed, the user must install them manually. If they are not installed, pause executing this prompt and ask the user to install them using the Visual Studio NuGet Package Manager or Visual Studio package manager console.
6. Modify `web.config` to add config builders in `configSections` and root; configure EnvironmentConfigBuilder for `appSettings` and `connectionStrings`:
`<section name="configBuilders" type="System.Configuration.ConfigurationBuildersSection, System.Configuration, Version=<REDACTED_IP>, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b03f5f7f11d50a3a" restartOnExternalChanges="false" requirePermission="false" />`
`<add name="Environment" type="Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.EnvironmentConfigBuilder, Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.Environment" />`
`<appSettings configBuilders="Environment">` (retain existing settings)
`<connectionStrings configBuilders="Environment">` (retain existing strings)
7. Create `LogMonitorConfig.json` in the Dockerfile folder by copying the reference below. The file's contents **MUST NOT** not be modified and should match the reference content exactly unless instructions in containerization settings specify otherwise. In particular, do not change the issue logging level; `Information` for EventLog sources creates unnecessary noise.
8. Create a root `Dockerfile` with multiple stages:
   - Build: Windows Server Core; build base MUST use `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/sdk` unless settings specify a custom image. Copy sln, csproj, and packages.config first; copy `NuGet.config` if present and configure private feeds; restore NuGet packages; copy remaining source; build and publish to `C:\publish` using MSBuild.
   - Runtime: selected Windows image; final base MUST use `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/aspnet` unless settings specify a custom image. Copy `LogMonitorConfig.json` into the image (e.g. `C:\LogMonitor`); download LogMonitor.exe from https://github.com/microsoft/windows-container-tools/releases/download/v2.1.1/LogMonitor.exe; set working directory to `C:\inetpub\wwwroot`; copy published output from `C:\publish`; configure entry point:
`ENTRYPOINT [ "C:\\LogMonitor\\LogMonitor.exe", "C:\\ServiceMonitor.exe", "w3svc" ]`
   Apply settings for SKU/version, user, GAC, COM, roles/features, and files. **IMPORTANT:** Use a Windows Server Core base image unless the user has **specifically requested** a full Windows Server image in the settings file.
9. Create root `.dockerignore`, including all additional settings patterns.
10. Add Dockerfile `HEALTHCHECK` if an endpoint is specified.
11. Add `<None Include="Dockerfile" />` to the project file.
12. Mark completed tasks `[ ]` → `[✓]`.
13. Continue until all tasks are complete and Docker build succeeds. Confirm build using:
`docker build -t aspnet-app:latest .`
If it fails, address errors in Dockerfile or project configuration and report success/failure.

Maintain `progress.md`:
[ ] .NET Framework version detection (version: ___)
[ ] Windows Server SKU selection (SKU: ___)
[ ] Windows Server version selection (Version: ___)
[ ] Web.config modifications for configuration builders
[ ] NuGet package source configuration (if applicable)
[ ] Copy LogMonitorConfig.json and adjust if required by settings
[ ] .dockerignore file creation
[ ] Build stage created with SDK image
[ ] sln, csproj, packages.config, and (if applicable) NuGet.config copied for package restore
[ ] Runtime stage created with runtime image
[ ] Non-root user configuration
[ ] Dependency handling (GAC, MSI, COM, registry, additional files, etc.)
[ ] Health check configuration (if applicable)
[ ] Special requirements implementation
[ ] Review containerization settings and make sure that all requirements are met
[ ] Docker build success

Do not pause for confirmation between steps. Continue methodically until the application has been containerized and Docker build succeeds.
**YOU ARE NOT DONE UNTIL ALL CHECKBOXES ARE MARKED!** This includes building the Docker image successfully and addressing any issues that arise during the build process.

Reference `LogMonitorConfig.json` contents:
"directory": "c:\\inetpub\\logs",
"providerName": "IIS: WWW Server",
"providerGuid": "3A2A4E84-4C21-4981-AE10-3F
